questions.question:
**Direction: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution’.**

Alice won’t be coming to the concert as **__she was__** ill.
questions.solution:
Here, the correct answer is "she is."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• Here, the error lies in the part **"she is"** of the sentence.
 
• The sentence** "Alice won’t be coming to the concert as she was ill"** is grammatically incorrect.
 
• We must change **"was" **to "is" to maintain consistency in verb tense.
 
• This change ensures that the verb tense remains in the present tense throughout the sentence.
 
• The correct answer is Option 2.

 

**Correct sentence**:* Alice won’t be coming to the concert as **she is**__ ill.*

questions.question:
In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which will improve the underlined part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select “No improvement”.

Subhash Palekar a farmer received the Padma Shri award this year__ in his campaign for zero budget __natural farming.

options.text: at his campaign with zero budget
for his campaign for zero budget
for his campaign to zero budget

questions.solution:
The correct solution is option 2 i.e. **for his campaign for zero budget.**

 [IMAGE: https://lh5.googleusercontent.com/2pwqSq5ph6_V_4RreQSjVc8VGchGTW2ZxWjFS545Q1cYsS5Fs8MsfDMaQe8bpbBLb2DctBPZiCUNndteRiIw9CElV07flM_r6n0VFH_Az_wv5ZuXUgdOCqz09Ywsrg3ORcVL_v4k] Explanation

__
 
• 'in his campaign for zero budget' is wrong because preposition 'in' is used to express the situation of something that is or appears to be enclosed or surrounded by something else.
 
• **'at' **is used to express location or arrival in a particular place or position.
 
• **'for'** is used to indicate the person or thing that something is sent or given to.
 
• **'to' **is used to express motion in the direction of (a particular location).
 
• Here, in the sentence, the Padma Shri indicates his great work in his campaign. So, 'for' is the most appropriate word. 

**Correct sentence:**__ Subhash Palekar a farmer received the Padma Shri award this year__ for his campaign for zero budget __natural farming.

questions.solution:

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"I wheeled a** recycling bin** to the curb."*

• **Recycling bins** – This would be incorrect because it suggests multiple bins, whereas the sentence refers to only one.
 
• **Recycled bins** – This is incorrect because "recycled" describes something that has been processed for reuse, not a bin for recycling.

questions.question:
**Directions: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.**

There will be __little more__ pupils in the class next year, but we have enough space.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**a few more**.'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the underlined segment, the use of the quantifier 'little' is incorrect.
 
• The quantifier 'little' means **not much or not enough**.
 
• The quantifier 'little' is used **with **uncountable nouns.
 
• The given sentence is talking about **a spacious classroom capable of accomodating some more pupils next year**.
 
• In the given sentence the **noun 'pupils'** is a **plural countable noun**.
 
• Therefore, the quantifier ''a few'' should be used in place of the quantifier 'little'.
 
• The quantifier ''a few'' is used **with ****plural** countable nouns.
 
• The quantifier ''a few'' means **somewhat (though not much). **It has a** positive meaning. **It is used in the context of **'some.'**

 

Hence, the correct answer is option 2.

Correct Sentence: *There will be **a few more pupils** in the class next year, but we have enough space*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• The quantifier 'much' is used **with uncountable nouns**, mainly **in negative sentences and questions**, or **after as, how, so, too**; **a large amount of something**. (किसी वस्‍तु की अधिक मात्रा)
 
• The quantifier 'few' is used **with **plural countable nouns but it means limited or below average; hardly any. It has a **negative meaning**. (सीमित या औसत से कम; शायद ही कोई)
 
• The quantifier 'a little' is used **with singular uncountable nouns** and it means **a small amount of something**. (किसी वस्‍तु की थोड़ी मात्रा, थोड़ी-सी)

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/51867102c7c2f369f6e29d2efe025e3b3367c68261ec20262828d84ca5c8f854.png] **Hinglish__**

__
 
• रेखांकित खण्ड में quantifier 'little' का प्रयोग गलत है।
 
• Quantifier 'little' का अर्थ "**अधिक या पर्याप्त नहीं" **होता** **है।
 
• Quantifier 'little' का प्रयोग uncountable nouns के साथ किया जाता है।
 
• दिया गया वाक्य **एक विशाल कक्षा के बारे में बात कर रहा है जो अगले साल कुछ और विद्यार्थियों को समायोजित करने में सक्षम है**।
 
• दिए गए वाक्य में noun 'pupils' एक plural countable noun है।
 
• इसलिए quantifier 'little' के स्थान पर quantifier ''a few'' का प्रयोग किया जाना चाहिए।
 
• Quantifier ''a few'' का प्रयोग plural countable nouns के साथ किया जाता है।
 
• Quantifier ''a few'' का अर्थ है **एक छोटी संख्या; कुछ; कुछ हद तक (हालांकि ज्यादा नहीं**)। इसका **सकारात्मक अर्थ **है। इसका प्रयोग '**some**' के संदर्भ में किया जाता है।

 

अत: सही उत्तर विकल्प 2 है।

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"Mount Everest."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"Those Mount Everests"** is incorrect as it refers to multiple mountains, whereas **Mount Everest **is singular.
 
• **"Mount Everest"** is a proper noun and cannot be preceded by an indefinite article.
 
 
• **Example**:* I may trek **Mount Everest**__.*
 
 
 
• The correct answer is Option 2.

 

**Correct sentence**: *__**Mount Everest**__ is Earth's highest mountain above sea level, located in the sub-range of the Himalayas.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Option 1, **"The Mount Everest"**, is grammatically incorrect as **"Mount Everest"** is already a proper noun and does not require an article.
 
• Option 4, **"A Mount Everest"**, is grammatically incorrect as **"Mount Everest"** is a proper noun and cannot be preceded by an indefinite article.

questions.question:
**Direction: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.**

Do you want / to visit a zoo / when you / go to Ahmedabad?
questions.solution:
Here, the erroneous part is **"to visit a zoo."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The segment** 'to visit a zoo' **is incorrect.
 
• The error lies in the use of the article** "a"** before the noun** "zoo."**
 
• Here, we are referring to the specific **"zoo,"** so must use **"the" **before the word **"zoo."**
 
• The correct sentence would be *"Do you want **to visit the zoo**__ when you go to Ahmedabad?"*
 
• The correct answer is Option 1.

questions.question:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose ‘No improvement’ as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

In the logo the blue __contrast wells __with its complementary colour, yellow:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**contrasts well**."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **The verb 'contrast' needs to agree with the subject 'blue', which is singular. **
 
• **Therefore, 'contrasts' is the correct form.**
 
• 'Well' is an adverb, which is used to modify a verb.
 
• In this case, it modifies 'contrasts' to indicate how well the blue and yellow colors complement each other.
 
• Thus, the correct phrase to use in the given sentence will be: "contrasts well."

Hence,** the correct answer is option 4.**

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution’.

Spreading awareness about the rights of the consumers and the relief open to them in case they __did not get their money’s worth __of goods and service has rightly been identified as the first priority.

options.text: do not get their money’s worth
did not getting their money’s worth
will not get their money’s worth

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**do not get their money’s worth**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"did not get"** is incorrect because the reporting clause is in present perfect tense ("has rightly been identified"), so the subordinate clause should remain in present tense.
 
• The correct substitution is **"do not get"**, which matches the present context and conveys an ongoing or possible situation.
 
• Additionally, "goods and service" should be corrected to **"goods and services"** for proper usage.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Complete Sentence:** *"Spreading awareness about the rights of the consumers and the relief open to them in case they **do not get their money’s worth of goods and services**__ has rightly been identified as the first priority."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: "No substitution"** is incorrect because "did not get" mismatches the tense of the main clause.
 
• **Option 3: "did not getting"** is grammatically wrong; the verb form is incorrect.
 
• **Option 4: "will not get"** is incorrect because it unnecessarily shifts the meaning to future tense, while the sentence is about present/ongoing situations.
